key_facts: This decision concerns the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix race on 13 September 2026.
Driver Gabriel Bortoleto (Car 5) of Audi Revolut F1 Team moved under braking when approaching Turn 5.
His car impacted Car 43, which was forced to leave the track.
Bortoleto breached Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 e) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
The Stewards issued a Warning, which is equivalent to a black/white flag (a penalty for unsportsmanlike or reckless driving).
summary.plain_explanation:
Gabriel Bortoleto, driving Car 5 for Audi Revolut F1 Team, was penalised during the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix race.

Under braking as he approached Turn 5, Bortoleto's car moved from its line and hit Car 43. The impact forced Car 43 off the track. This kind of movement under braking is prohibited. The rules say drivers must not move in a sudden, dangerous way while braking, because it can cause collisions and put other drivers in danger.

The Stewards reviewed video evidence and gave Bortoleto a Warning. This is equivalent to a black/white flag, which is the baseline penalty for this type of infringement.

key_facts: Driver Charles Leclerc in car 16 for Scuderia Ferrari was penalised during the race at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix.
Both cars entered turn 4 with excessive speed and neither could have made the corner while staying on track.
Car 16 left the track and gained a lasting advantage by completing an overtake whilst off track, breaching Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
The Stewards applied a 5 second time penalty, reduced from the baseline guideline of 10 seconds because car 44 was also off track and the incident occurred early in the first lap.
summary.plain_explanation:
Charles Leclerc in car 16 for Scuderia Ferrari was given a 5 second time penalty during the race at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix.

The Stewards reviewed video evidence and positioning data. At turn 4 early in the first lap, both car 16 and car 44 entered with excessive speed. Neither car could have stayed on the track through the corner. Car 44 was on the inside and had to go off track. Car 16 then completed an overtake while off track and gained a lasting advantage.

This breached Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations, which requires drivers to stay on track. The Stewards normally apply a 10 second penalty for this infringement, but reduced it to 5 seconds because car 44 was also off track and this happened very early in the race.

key_facts: Charles Leclerc (car 16) driving for Scuderia Ferrari HP breached Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations in the race at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix.

summary.plain_explanation:
Charles Leclerc was given a 5 second time penalty in the race at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix.

At turn 4 on the first lap, Leclerc's car entered the corner too fast to stay on the track. The other car (car 44, on the inside) also had to go off track because both cars were going too fast to make the corner. Leclerc then completed an overtake while he was off the track. This breached Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations, which prevents drivers from leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage.

The stewards said the baseline penalty guideline for this breach is 10 seconds. However, they reduced it to 5 seconds because the other car was also off track on the inside of Leclerc's car, and because the incident happened early in the first lap.

summary.plain_explanation:
During the race at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix, the stewards reviewed evidence about an incident involving Charles Leclerc in car 16 and another car, car 44, at turn 4.

Both cars entered turn 4 with excessive speed and therefore could not make the corner while staying on track. Car 44 had to go off track because it was on the inside. Car 16 then completed an overtake while off track, which is not allowed.

Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations prohibits leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage. This is what Leclerc did. The stewards determined he was not entitled to claim the corner because of the excessive entry speed, and by overtaking while off track he breached the regulation.

The stewards gave Leclerc a 5 second time penalty. The baseline penalty guideline for this kind of breach is 10 seconds, but they reduced it because car 44 was also off track on the inside and because this happened early in the first lap.

key_facts: The decision concerns car 30, driven by Liam Lawson of the Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team, in qualifying at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix on 31 October 2026.

Car 30 breached Articles C5.12.6 and C5.12.7 of the F1 Regulations, which set requirements for how the MGUK (a motor-generator unit for kinetic energy) must be deployed and stepped down after the control line at the end of a qualifying lap.

After the control line at the end of his fastest lap in Q2, Liam Lawson did not immediately lift off the power, with the result that the car did not achieve the required rate of reduction of MGUK deployment.

The team argued no performance advantage was gained, but the Stewards noted that non-compliance with the Technical Regulations is not excused by lack of performance advantage, and that cars must comply at all times during an event.
Car 30 is disqualified from the results of the Provisional Qualifying Classifications.
summary.plain_explanation:
Liam Lawson's car failed to comply with the technical regulations during qualifying at the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. After crossing the control line at the end of his fastest lap in Q2, Lawson did not immediately lift off the power. This meant the car's MGUK — a motor-generator unit that recovers kinetic energy — was not stepped down (reduced) at the rate the regulations require.

The Racing Bulls team said this gave them no advantage in performance. But the Stewards explained that the regulations do not allow non-compliance even without a performance gain. Cars must follow the technical regulations at all times during an event. The team did disclose the breach themselves, which the Stewards noted, but the Stewards said there are many previous decisions that require them to disqualify a car for breach of the technical regulations, whatever the circumstances.

As a result, car 30 is disqualified from the results of qualifying.

The car breached the Technical Regulations in two articles that control the Motor Generator Unit Kinetic, or MGUK. This is a system that recovers energy and feeds it back into the car. The regulations require that after the control line at the end of a lap, the driver must lift off the power immediately. This triggers a step down, a controlled reduction in MGUK deployment.

On Lawson's fastest lap in Q2, after he crossed the control line, he did not lift off the power straight away. As a result, the car did not achieve the required rate of reduction in MGUK deployment that the regulations demand.

The Racing Bulls team argued that this breach did not give the car any performance advantage. However, the Stewards ruled that the Technical Regulations must be followed at all times, and a breach is a breach even if no advantage was gained. The Stewards noted that the team disclosed the problem themselves, which is a point in their favour. But the Stewards found that previous decisions require disqualification when a car does not comply with the Technical Regulations, and so the disqualification is imposed.

They also noted that the regulations require a car to comply with them at all times during an event.

Although the team self-disclosed the breach, the Stewards said there are many precedents that require disqualification when a car does not comply with the Technical Regulations, regardless of other circumstances.

key_facts: This document sets out Race Director's instructions for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix, 30 October – 1 November 2026.

The notes cover general matters including qualifying laps, lapping during the race, and safety car procedures, plus competition-specific instructions on parc fermé access, pit lane rules, grid procedures and track limits.
Drivers must allow faster cars past at the first available opportunity when caught; blue light panels will show when the faster car is within 1.2 seconds.

Any driver exceeding the maximum time between two safety car lines during qualifying laps, in-laps, out-laps or reconnaissance laps may be deemed to be going unnecessarily slowly and subject to investigation.

The document specifies numerous track limit rules: drivers missing the apex at Turn 4 must rejoin via a specific asphalt route; drivers whose car passes completely behind the red and white kerb at Turn 11 must rejoin by a specified polystyrene block arrangement.
Safety Car deployment and withdrawal will be signalled only by messages to competitors and trackside light panels, not by waved yellow flags or SC boards.
summary.plain_explanation:
These are the Race Director's Competition Notes for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. They contain instructions for teams and drivers covering how to conduct themselves during free practice, qualifying, and the race.

On qualifying laps, drivers cannot go unnecessarily slowly between the Second Safety Car Line and the First Safety Car Line. This applies to qualifying session laps, in-laps and out-laps, and reconnaissance laps before the race. Drivers who exceed the maximum time on any of these laps may be investigated and penalized. The maximum time will be announced after the second practice session.

During the race, drivers who are caught by faster cars must allow them to pass at the first available opportunity. The marshalling system will give the slower car's team a pre-warning when the faster car is within 3.0 seconds. When the faster car comes within 1.2 seconds, blue light panels (along with blue cockpit lights and messages on timing monitors) will be shown to the slower car to tell the driver to let the other car through.

The notes detail where team personnel can access the parc fermé (the sealed area where cars are held after qualifying and the race). For the race, cars selected for the podium ceremony will stop at Turn 13 under parc fermé conditions. All other cars will go to the pit lane parc fermé area. Personnel for cars not selected for the podium can enter parc fermé by a marked blue route.

The document explains how the marshalling system works at pit entry and exit. A car entering the pit lane is subject to the yellow or double yellow flag conditions of the sector until it passes a marked blue line. A car leaving the pit lane is subject to the marshalling conditions of the sector it is entering after it passes the blue line.

Practice starts are allowed during free practice and reconnaissance laps but not during qualifying. During reconnaissance laps before the race, cars wishing to perform a practice start must leave the pit lane and stay to the right, without crossing a white line into the circuit. They may stop in the area before Safety Car Line 2 to perform the practice start, then rejoin via the pit exit road.

On track limits: if a driver misses the apex at Turn 4, enters the run-off area, and crosses the yellow line with all four wheels, they must rejoin the circuit after Turn 5 using an asphalt rejoin route. Drivers may use the grass only if clearly unavoidable. If a driver's car passes completely behind the red and white kerb at the apex of Turn 11, they must rejoin by keeping to the right of the first polystyrene block arrangement and then to the left of the second polystyrene block. At Turn 17, failing to negotiate the turn properly may result in the lap time and the immediately following lap time being invalidated.

The Safety Car procedures have changed for this event. Waved yellow flags and SC boards will not be used. When the Safety Car is deployed, the message "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" will be sent and all trackside light panels will display "SC". When the Safety Car lights are turned off, the message "SAFETY CAR LIGHTS OFF" will be sent. As the leader approaches the Control Line, a green light panel will be displayed and other panels will clear. If the Safety Car is still deployed at the beginning of the last lap or is deployed during the last lap, it will enter the pit lane at the end of the lap and cars must proceed to the end-of-session signal without overtaking before the Control Line.

The notes also include various procedural details on pit lane access times, grid procedures, removing cars from the grid, and race suspension procedures.

summary.plain_explanation:
This document sets out the rules and procedures for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. It covers many different aspects of how the race weekend will be run, from practice sessions through to the race itself.

During qualifying and the reconnaissance laps before the race (a warm-up lap where the pit exit is opened), drivers must not take longer than a maximum time to drive between two safety car lines on the track. If they do, they may be investigated for going unnecessarily slowly. The teams will be told what this maximum time is after the second practice session.

When a faster driver is catching up to a driver who will be lapped (a slower driver who has already been passed and is a full lap or more behind), blue flag signals will be shown to warn the slower driver. The slower driver must then let the faster driver pass at the first opportunity they can safely do so.

The document explains where team personnel can go in parc fermé, which is the area where the cars are kept under strict control. Different routes are used after qualifying than after the race, and personnel who work on cars for the podium ceremony (the ceremony for the top three finishers) wait in a separate area.

Practice starts (test starts that drivers do to prepare for the actual race start) have detailed rules. Drivers can do them in specific areas during free practice and reconnaissance laps, but not during qualifying. The document shows where these areas are and which rules apply.

There are also specific rules about which parts of the track are considered "in bounds" (within the allowed racing area) at certain corners. For example, at Turn 17, if a driver does not take the correct line, their lap time and the next lap time may be cancelled. At Turn 4, if a driver goes off the track and fully crosses a yellow line, they must rejoin using a specific asphalt (paved) route rather than grass.

The document explains how safety car (a car that paces the field when there is an incident or danger on track) procedures will work. Instead of waved yellow flags, the message "SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED" will be sent electronically to all teams and drivers, and light panels on the track will display "SC". When the safety car is about to leave at the end of a lap, teams will get the message "SAFETY CAR LIGHTS OFF" and drivers must not overtake before the control line (the line that marks the end of the safety car period).

Finally, the document lists changes that have been made to the Mexico City circuit itself, including areas that have been resurfaced, new painted lines, and the new position of the practice start boxes.

This document sets out the Race Director's competition notes for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. It covers how officials and teams must run the event safely and fairly.

Drivers must not go unnecessarily slowly on the circuit. If a driver exceeds the maximum time between the Second and First Safety Car Lines on any lap during qualifying, in-laps, out-laps, or reconnaissance laps, the stewards may investigate them. key_facts: This document applies to all teams and officials at the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix on 13-15 March 2026.
The Race Director sets out rules for safe and orderly conduct during practice sessions, Sprint Qualifying, Qualifying, Sprint, and Race.
Drivers must not exceed maximum times between Safety Car lines during qualifying and reconnaissance laps, or they may be deemed to be going unnecessarily slowly.

summary.plain_explanation:
This document gives instructions for the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix to make sure the race and qualifying sessions run safely and fairly.

The Race Director explains when drivers go too slowly. Any driver who takes longer than the maximum time between the Second Safety Car Line and the First Safety Car Line during Sprint Qualifying, Qualifying, or reconnaissance laps may be judged to be going unnecessarily slowly. This can happen on any lap, including laps when a driver comes into or leaves the pit lane. Teams will be told what the maximum time is after practice.

During the Sprint and Race, the rules require drivers who are caught by a faster car to let that car pass as soon as possible. If a faster car gets within 1.2 seconds of a slower car, blue light panels will be shown as a signal. The driver of the slower car must then let the faster driver through at the first chance.

The document sets out rules for pit lane safety. Team staff can only be in the pit lane just before they need to work on a car, and must leave as soon as the work is finished. After the race ends and all cars have entered the Parc Fermé area (a controlled parking area where cars stay), the Race Director will send a message saying pit lane access rules no longer apply.

Practice starts are only allowed on the grid or pit exit road during specific times. Drivers cannot do practice starts during Sprint Qualifying, Qualifying, or during the actual Sprint or Race. When reconnaissance laps happen before the Sprint or Race, drivers can do practice starts by stopping at a white line at pit exit, but they must not cross another white line and must stay in the correct part of the pit exit road.

The document explains pit entry and pit exit procedures. Drivers must follow marked white lines. At pit exit, drivers can only use the line painted on the track at pit exit and the line continuing after the Second Safety Car line.

Starting procedures require grid light panels to flash blue for 5 seconds before the lights go out for the start. After any standing start or restart, Driver Adjustable Bodywork in straight mode will be enabled after Turn 1.

Other rules cover when sessions can be stopped, how drivers must be weighed after qualifying, where cars can be removed from the grid, and where fire extinguishers and emergency equipment are located on the circuit. The document also notes small changes to the circuit, including a lower kerb at Turn 3 and moved tyre barriers.

Teams and drivers must follow these instructions together with the FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations.
summary.plain_explanation:
These are the Competition Notes for the 2026 Chinese Grand Prix, issued by the FIA Formula One Race Director on 12 March 2026. They give teams and drivers detailed instructions for the safe and orderly running of the event.

The notes explain how drivers must behave during practice, sprint qualifying, qualifying, and the race. For example, when a driver is being lapped (caught by a faster car), they must allow the faster driver past at the first available opportunity. The marshalling system will warn drivers: when the faster car is within 3.0 seconds, the team should prepare their driver; when the faster car is within 1.2 seconds, blue light panels will be shown and the driver must let the other car pass.

Pit lane safety receives detailed attention. Team personnel are only allowed in the pit lane when they are immediately required to work on a car, and must leave as soon as the work is done. A specific message will be sent when this rule no longer applies after the race ends.

The notes cover starting procedures. Before the start or restart of the sprint or race, the grid lights will flash blue for 5 seconds, followed by the standard light sequence. After a standing start or restart, driver adjustable bodywork will be enabled after Turn 1.

Practice starts have specific rules. They cannot be done at pit exit, and during reconnaissance laps (test laps before the race), drivers wishing to practice a start must stay to the left-hand side of the pit exit road and not cross the white line painted there. Drivers who do not want to practice a start must cross the white line and join the normal racing line.

The notes also cover lapping (being lapped by a faster car). When a driver is caught by another car, the marshalling system will give warnings: first when the faster car is 3.0 seconds behind, then with blue light panels when it is 1.2 seconds behind. The slower driver must then let the faster driver overtake at the first opportunity.

When the safety car is about to return to the pits, from the moment the orange lights on the safety car go out, drivers must not brake or accelerate suddenly, or make any manoeuvre that could endanger other drivers or disrupt the restart.

Several technical checks are required. Each morning before practice, teams must connect telemetry equipment to check the car's ERS (energy recovery system) safety status. If a car's ERS is in a Hazard Status (unsafe condition), the team must send mechanics to a collection point after the session.

The notes set out rules for which lap times count. Only lap times completed on the track will be counted for any classification.

The circuit itself has some changes. The kerb at Turn 3 is lower, the tyre barrier at Turn 7 has been moved, and a trackside panel called TSP 17 before Turn 14 has been moved 100 metres further back.

The notes also explain the locations of key features: pit entry and exit, grid removal gates, fire extinguishers, and where cars can be removed from the track in an emergency.
